node-1.label: Multiple 1- to 2-mm shiny papules on the upper limbs and body, with coalescence into plaques on the untreated arm

node-2.label: Patient is a man in his 40s with a history of metastatic lung adenocarcinoma, previously treated with 2 courses of radiotherapy to head and leg and 4 cycles of carboplatin, pemetrexed, and bevacizumab, followed by nivolumab (3 mg/kg) every 2 weeks.

node-3.label: After 8 cycles of nivolumab over 5 months, he developed 1- to 2-mm shiny papules on the upper limbs, which spread to the rest of the body over the subsequent 3 months.

node-5.label: Physical examination revealed multiple 1- to 2-mm shiny papules scattered on the upper limbs and body, with lesions on the untreated arm coalescing into plaques.

attrs.why: The biopsy results from both the Laboratory Physician and Pathologist confirm focal lymphohistiocytic infiltrates with vacuolar interface changes and melanin incontinence, which are classic features of interface dermatitis and strongly support an immune-related drug reaction. This histopathological evidence, combined with the temporal onset after 8 nivolumab cycles and pruritus, definitively confirms nivolumab-induced cutaneous reaction, raising confidence from 0.82 to 0.95.

The biopsy findings showing interface dermatitis without atypical epithelioid cells directly exclude metastatic carcinoma. Both the Laboratory Physician and Pathologist explicitly confirm that the histopathology rules out metastatic spread. Combined with the strong temporal link to nivolumab, metastatic cutaneous spread is now highly unlikely, reducing confidence from 0.12 to 0.03.

The histopathological findings of interface dermatitis with vacuolar changes and melanin incontinence are classic for drug-induced lichenoid/interface dermatitis, not typical of infectious or inflammatory dermatoses. Both experts confirm that the biopsy supports an immune-related drug reaction, and the immunotherapy context and timeline further refute infectious or inflammatory causes, reducing confidence from 0.06 to 0.02.
